<description>
The `sock_tests/send_and_receive` unit test can fail in the -- improbable -- case when network reads happen to arrive in smaller chunks.

Related to #36726 .

All networking code using sockets must not make assumption about the chunking of the incoming/outgoing data, and should be resilient against any chunking.

This test expects to read 4 bytes from the socket, and it expects that to happen in one `Recv()` call. However, there is no guarantee that data arrives in one call.

This was found -- and can be reproduced -- by using a reproducer patch, that forces all socket sends to use smaller chunking. For the run with the reproducer see #36751 .

The issue is test-code only, the non-test code is correct.

The fix is to replace the single `Recv` call with one or more repeated calls, until the expected amount of data is read, and do the checks only afterwards.

This fix makes the test more robust, even though a failure due to this issue in CI is very unlikely, but not impossible.
</description>

<commits>
baf2e9df91 test: sock_tests: Handle partial reads in send_and_receive

In `sock_tests/send_and_receive`, replace a single `Recv` call with
one or more repeated calls, until the expected amount of data is read,
and do the checks only afterwards.
There is no guarantee that the expected data is returned in one call,
even if it is written in one `send()`, and even on a loopback
connection, hence the need for the loop.
</commits>

<files>
src/test/sock_tests.cpp  +8/-1

(test/bench/ci lines: 9)
</files>

<patch>
diff --git a/src/test/sock_tests.cpp b/src/test/sock_tests.cpp
index d9ebc4af5f..fd70a6fc08 100644
--- a/src/test/sock_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/sock_tests.cpp
@@ -129,7 +129,14 @@ struct TcpSocketPair {
         char recv_buf[10];
 
         BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(sender.Send(msg, msg_len, 0), msg_len);
-        BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(receiver.Recv(recv_buf, sizeof(recv_buf), 0), msg_len);
+        // TCP may deliver the data in several pieces
+        ssize_t received{0};
+        while (received < msg_len) {
+            const ssize_t ret{receiver.Recv(recv_buf + received, sizeof(recv_buf) - received, 0)};
+            BOOST_REQUIRE_GT(ret, 0);
+            received += ret;
+        }
+        BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(received, msg_len);
         BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(strncmp(msg, recv_buf, msg_len), 0);
     }
 };

</patch>
